title: laplace.packet-judgement/1
description: The ONE shape an independent judge returns, for every provider. It merges the shape Codex root settled on (evidence/WRITING_CONSOLIDATION_2026-10-03/resume-codex-20261003/canonical_action-judge.json and delivery_gate-judge2.json: schema_version, round, max_rounds, candidate/parent/base/tree, accepted_subsets with id/status/finding, contested subsets with their minimum correction, independent_evidence) with the closure-loop rule that a deficiency says what done looks like. The judge's own commands are the acceptance evidence: the carrier already refuses an acceptance with no successful command of the judge's own (src/laplace/pipeline/workflow.py:811-813, ADVERSARY-HAS-NO-INDEPENDENT-COMMAND-OBSERVATION), and check-return applies that same rule to this file.

schema_version.description: This schema's $id; the version check-return resolves the validating schema by.

packet.description: The label of the packet being judged, verbatim from the plan.

round.description: Which judgement round this is, 1-based; it is part of the verdict file name and of the banked row id.

max_rounds.description: The plan's max_judge_rounds: after this round the orchestrator rules instead of the judge.

accepted.description: The verdict. True is only legal with at least one own_observations entry whose exit_code is 0 and with no deficiencies.

judged.description: Exactly what was judged, so the judgement is about a commit and not about a transcript.

candidate.description: The commit the judge checked out, which must equal the return's source.candidate.

review_checkout.description: Absolute path of the judge's OWN checkout; judging the builder's worktree is judging the builder's state.

scripted_check.description: The packet's scripted check re-run by the judge in its own checkout, with its exit code.

command.description: The exact command line the judge ran.

exit_code.description: The process exit status as the judge observed it.

checked.description: The sample the judge actually read or ran, item by item: the plan's judge_sample is a floor on this list's length, not a suggestion.

item.description: The claim or file:line that was checked.

how.description: The command run or the lines read that checked it.

accepted_subsets.description: The parts of the work that stand, each with the finding that establishes it; a rejection is still a record of what was accepted.

id.description: A stable id for this subset, so round two can be read against round one.

status.description: ACCEPTED when the judge's own observation establishes it; CONTESTED when it does not.

finding.description: What the judge observed, with the file:line or command that observed it.

deficiencies.description: What blocks acceptance. Non-empty requires accepted false; each entry says what done looks like, so the continuation has a target instead of a complaint.

id.description: A stable id, carried into the continuation and into round two.

item.description: The file:line, command or claim the deficiency is about.

problem.description: What is wrong, stated as a defect and not as a preference.

evidence.description: The judge's own observation that shows it.

done_looks_like.description: The checkable state that would close this deficiency.

own_observations.description: Commands the judge ran itself, with exit codes: the independence evidence. An acceptance needs at least one with exit_code 0.

command.description: The exact command run in the judge's own checkout.
